label: sec:intro#souza-claro
statement: In the two-dimensional two-electron Hubbard problem, the repulsively bound pair forms a distinct U-band and behaves dynamically as a charge-2e composite object.

label: sec:intro#nonclaim-novelty
statement: The paper does not claim as new: the mapping of correlated few-particle problems onto higher-dimensional single-particle lattices and the coordinate counting built on it; the Fock-space/configuration-graph hopping language; the strong-coupling no-double-occupancy projection and spectral-moment methods; or the closed-walk-to-permutation-cycle connection (a closed walk permutes the background spins, which are restored iff every nontrivial cycle is spin-uniform).

label: sec:benchmark#doublonH
statement: At fixed total momentum and every U, the two-electron relative-coordinate equation is exactly the Koster-Slater bound state at a repulsive defect; to leading order in $\lambda/U$ the pair is a composite boson hopping on the same LxL lattice with $E_{\rm pair}(K)\approx\varepsilon_d+2t_d(\cos K_x+\cos K_y)$, $\varepsilon_d=U+8\lambda^2/U$, $t_d=2\lambda^2/U$.

label: sec:benchmark#doublonsign
statement: The sign of the doublon hopping is fixed, not a convention: exactly two second-order virtual paths connect adjacent doublon sites, each contributing $+\lambda^2/U$ with no additional fermion sign, so the doublon band is inverted relative to a bare particle (maximum at K=0); since $d_r\to e^{2i\theta_r}d_r$, the staggered bipartite gauge transformation that flips the bare hopping sign leaves the doublon sign unchanged.

label: sec:benchmark#claro-robles
statement: In the exact one-dimensional two-electron solution, the repulsively bound-pair dispersion has strong-coupling expansion $E_{\rm pair}=\varepsilon_d+2t_d\cos K_{\rm CM}+O(\lambda^4/U^3)$ with $t_d=2\lambda^2/U$ (used as independent exact corroboration of the positive doublon-hopping sign), and the pair shows a doubled Bloch-oscillation frequency under an applied field, identified as a dynamical signature of composite charge 2e.

label: sec:benchmark#closure
statement: With zero fitted parameters, at U=10,15,20 lambda on the L=7 lattice, the predicted U-band centre $\varepsilon_d$ matches the exact two-electron mean to within 0.06% and the predicted band edge $\varepsilon_d+4t_d$ matches the observed maximum to within 0.5%; the centre test and the DOS collapse are insensitive to the sign of $t_d$ on any lattice, while at odd L=7 the band edge favours the derived sign (deviations 0.45%, 0.11%, 0.04% against 1.14%, 0.44%, 0.23% for the opposite sign).
source: checks/slow_finite_U.py; evidence/2026-11-13-finite-U (closure_L7: exact diagonalization of all 2401 states, U=10,15,20)

label: fig:ubandcollapse
statement: For several U, the exact two-electron U-band collapses onto the single predicted 2D doublon dispersion once rescaled by $t_d$ and $\varepsilon_d$, both predicted directly from U and lambda with no fitted parameters.

label: sec:benchmark#nonclaim-doublonform
statement: The functional form of the perturbative doublon Hamiltonian is not claimed as new (comparable effective doublon Hamiltonians exist for an extended, mass-imbalanced Hubbard model and for a periodically driven one), nor is its doubled Peierls phase; the stated contributions are its explicit derivation on any graph (second-order terms machine-checked for the two-electron problem) and the zero-fitted-parameter connection to the exact two-electron U-band.

label: sec:clusters#freeconfig
statement: For every n, ignoring interactions and exchange, n particles on a 2D lattice are exactly a single particle hopping on a 2n-dimensional hypercubic lattice, $\rho_n^{(0)}(E)=\rho_{2nD}(E)$; in particular two free (U=0) electrons are a single particle on a 4D hypercubic lattice with additive dispersion $E=-2\lambda\sum_{\alpha=1}^4\cos k_\alpha$.

label: sec:clusters#nonclaim-dcl
statement: $d_{\rm cl}$ is used only as a coordinate-counting dimension (the number of real-space coordinates needed to translate C objects in 2D); it is not the many-body Hilbert-space dimension, the spectral dimension of the configuration graph, or a scaling dimension, and coordinate counting alone is not claimed as a dynamical result.

label: sec:clusters#rule
statement: If n particles in two dimensions organize into C independently mobile clusters ($n=n_1+\dots+n_C$), each carrying exactly one 2D centre-of-mass coordinate, then $d_{\rm cl}=2C$ (codimension $2(n-C)$), each pairwise on-site constraint removing two dimensions.

label: sec:clusters#hubbard-rule
statement: In the single-band Hubbard model, which forbids on-site clusters larger than two, composites built purely from doublons plus unpaired electrons obey $d_{\rm cl}=2(n-N_d)$.

label: sec:fewbody#sectordim
statement: For all N, a, b, k, the number of configurations of a up-spin and b down-spin electrons on N sites with exactly k doubly occupied sites is $\binom{N}{a}\binom{a}{k}\binom{N-a}{b-k}$.

label: sec:fewbody#centres

label: sec:mu2theorem#regular
statement: For every z-regular graph, in particular the LxL square-lattice torus (z=4), $\mu_2(U\to\infty)=\lambda^2\,n\,z\,(N-n)/(N-1)$, independent of spin composition.

label: sec:mu2theorem#weighted
statement: For every spin-independent Hermitian weighted hopping matrix $H_t=-\sum_{i\ne j,\sigma}t_{ij}c^\dagger_{i\sigma}c_{j\sigma}$ ($t_{ji}=t_{ij}^*$, no on-site terms) on N>=2 sites and every n<=N, $\mu_2(U\to\infty)=\frac{n(N-n)}{N(N-1)}\sum_{i\ne j}|t_{ij}|^2$, independent of spin composition: the squared Frobenius norm of the off-diagonal part of the one-body hopping matrix T=(t_ij) times the combinatorial blocking probability.

label: sec:mu2theorem#fermionic
statement: The second-moment theorem and its weighted form hold for $H_\infty=P_0H_tP_0$ built from fermion operators satisfying the canonical anticommutation relations, for any spin-independent Hermitian hopping amplitudes (in particular any Peierls phases) and any ordering of the orbitals (which fixes the fermionic signs).

label: sec:fermistats#slater
statement: At U=0, for a single spin species, the many-body spectrum of k non-interacting fermions on N sites is exactly the set of sums over every choice of k distinct single-particle states (whose energies may be degenerate) without replacement (Slater determinants).

label: sec:fermistats#bandvariance

label: sec:fermistats#fpcvariance

label: sec:fermistats#U0-equals-Uinf

label: sec:mu4exchange#spinconditions
statement: Among length-4 closed walks in the N_d=0 configuration graph, identity-type walks (Type I single-particle excursions and Type II(a) walks in which two particles each return, possibly sharing an intermediate site) are spin-blind, depending only on (n,N); a transposition (Type II(b) ring exchange) returns to the identical occupation-number state iff both particles have the same spin, and a 3-cycle (Type III) iff all three do, contributing terms proportional to $P_{\rm same}$ and $P_3$ respectively.

label: sec:mu4exchange#channels
statement: On the LxL torus with L=3 or L>=5, ring exchange proceeds through exactly two geometrically distinct channels of equal weight, diagonal (next-nearest-neighbour pairs sharing two common neighbours, 2+2 hops) and edge (nearest-neighbour pairs, 3+1 hops around an adjacent plaquette); at n=2 each eligible pair contributes $-8\lambda^4$, derived by a complete fermion-sign count of every contributing path; 2N pairs in each channel.

label: sec:mu4exchange#alpha2-numeric

label: sec:mu4exchange#fourhop
statement: On any graph without self-loops, a closed walk of four hard-core hops induces on the particles only the identity, a transposition or a 3-cycle (a 4-cycle or double transposition would need a 1+1+1+1 hop schedule with no legal first move); more generally a closed walk of h hops moves no particle or fewer than h; a transposition and a 3-cycle both occur in four hops on every LxL torus with L>=3.

label: sec:mu4exchange#P3affine
statement: For every n, $P_3=\binom{N_\uparrow}{3}+\binom{N_\downarrow}{3}$ is an exact affine function of $P_{\rm same}$ at fixed $n=N_\uparrow+N_\downarrow$: $P_3=\binom{n}{3}-\frac{n-2}{2}\big[\binom{n}{2}-P_{\rm same}\big]$.

label: sec:mu4exchange#linearity
statement: On any finite graph, for every particle number n with two spin species, $\mu_4(U\to\infty)$ is exactly affine in the same-spin pair count at fixed (N,n), $\mu_4=A(N,n)+\alpha(N,n)P_{\rm same}$ (units of $\lambda^4$), with $\alpha=-T_2/\binom n2+(n-2)T_3/(2\binom n3)$ in terms of the average numbers of transposition and 3-cycle walks: proved from first principles (four-hop permutation bound, spin-averaging over labellings, and the $P_3$ identity), not an empirical observation.

label: sec:mu4exchange#proposition

label: sec:SW#Heff
statement: With $H=H_t+UD$, through third order the only virtual sector reached from the N_d=0 sector is N_d=1, so the Hermitian Schrieffer-Wolff expansion gives $H_{\rm eff}=T_0-\frac1U V+\frac1{U^2}H^{(3)}+O(1/U^3)$ with $T_0=P_0H_tP_0$, $T_1=Q_1H_tP_0$, $V=T_1^\dagger T_1$, $H^{(3)}=T_1^\dagger T_0^QT_1-\frac12\{V,T_0\}$, $T_0^Q=Q_1H_tQ_1$.

label: sec:SW#centralmoment
statement: With $\langle X\rangle=\mathrm{Tr}X/D_0$, the mean energy is $\bar E(U)=-\langle V\rangle/U+O(1/U^2)$ and the central second moment is $\mu_{2,c}(U)=\mu_2(\infty)-\frac2U\langle T_0V\rangle+\frac{c_2}{U^2}+O(1/U^3)$ with $c_2=\mathrm{Var}(V)+2\langle T_0H^{(3)}\rangle$.

label: sec:SW#crossterm
statement: On any triangle-free graph $\mathrm{Tr}(T_0V)=0$ (in the proof each term vanishes, needing a triangle); the LxL torus (L>=3) is triangle-free exactly when L is not 3, so for L>=4 the second-order correction operator V is exactly Hilbert-Schmidt orthogonal to the projected kinetic operator and $\mu_{2,c}$ has no 1/U term (a proven cancellation, not a fit).

label: sec:SW#c2-ED
statement: Full exact diagonalization of the Hubbard model at L=4 reproduces c2 for (1,1) and (2,1) to better than 1e-3 relative (Richardson extrapolation of U^2 (mu_2c(U)-mu_2(inf)) from U=400, 800); Var(V) alone has the wrong sign.

label: sec:SW#c2-sign
statement: In every low-filling sector computed (n<=5 at L=4,5,6) the third-order overlap is larger than Var(V) and of opposite sign, so c2<0 and the N_d=0 band narrows at large finite U; near half filling the sign reverses (at half filling T0=0 and c2=Var(V)>0; at L=4, c2(13,1)=6848/1575 and c2(12,2)=23424/2275 are positive). For n=2, c2(1,1)=-96/(N-1)-64/(N-1)^2 exactly at L=5..8 (computed, not derived).

label: sec:SW#beta-trend
statement: At low filling, c2/(N_up N_down) is close to composition-independent at fixed (L,n), with relative spread (|difference|/mean) shrinking as L grows: 0.14%, 0.06%, 0.03% between (3,1) and (2,2) at L=4,5,6 (n=4), and 0.34%, 0.13% between (4,1) and (3,2) at L=4,5 (n=5); the near-independence degrades with filling (0.79% between (5,1) and (3,3) at L=4, n=6) and c2 changes sign near half filling: numerical evidence that at low filling the U^-2 coefficient is governed by the opposite-spin pair count, c2 ~ beta(L,n) N_up N_down with beta<0.

label: tab:hierarchy#analytic
statement: Summary of the hierarchy: $\mu_2(\infty)$ resolves a directed edge, has no spin sensitivity and is exactly flux-blind for any flux; $\mu_4(\infty)$ resolves closed 4-hop loops, is exactly affine in $P_{\rm same}$ and responds as $\cos\Phi_\square$ (h/e), exchange changing parity, not charge; the Schrieffer-Wolff doublon hop is a composite two-link hop of the charge-2e pair sector with phase $e^{2iA_{ij}}$ and a pi-periodic twist (h/2e).

label: tab:hierarchy#finiteU
statement: The finite-U regime (virtual doublon excursion $T_1$ at cost U) is, at low filling and numerically, sensitive to the opposite-spin count N_up N_down, and has not yet been examined under flux.
source: sw_correction.py; checks/run_checks.py (sec:SW#beta: c2/(N_up N_down) trend; see sec:SW#beta-trend)

label: fig:conceptual
statement: Schematic of the microscopic origin of the hierarchy: single allowed hops from an occupied site to empty neighbours fix the spin-blind $\mu_2$; two geometrically distinct four-hop closed paths (diagonal 2+2, edge 3+1) return the occupied site set to itself, and to the same occupation-number state only for same spin, making $\mu_4$ exchange-sensitive; the virtual hop $T_1$ onto an opposite-spin site (cost U) and its return generate the leading finite-U correction to $\mu_2$.
source: schematic drawn in TikZ in manuscript/paper.tex (no script); content from analytic_studies/03_mu2_exact_theorem.tex §2, analytic_studies/05_mu4_exchange_topology.tex §3-§5, analytic_studies/07_schrieffer_wolff.tex §2

label: sec:discussion#nonclaim-alpha
statement: Eq. alphaN is stated for finite simple graphs; no claim is made for graphs with self-loops or multiple edges, nor for coefficients of higher moments.

label: sec:discussion#open-beta
statement: The paper does not derive beta(L,n), the prefactor of N_up N_down in the U^-2 coefficient c2 of $\mu_2$, nor the sign of c2; c2 itself is an exact trace for every composition, but its sign and the law c2 ~ beta(L,n) N_up N_down at low filling are numerical (at fixed n, |beta| is at most of order 1/N by the bound in annex 07 §6), epistemically distinct from the exact $\mu_2(\infty)$ theorem and the exact vanishing of the 1/U term.
source: analytic_studies/07_schrieffer_wolff.tex §6 (bound |c2| <= C(n,z) lambda^4 N_up N_down/(N-1)); checks/run_checks.py (sec:SW#beta)

label: sec:discussion#nonclaims
statement: Dedicated non-claims paragraph: beta(L,n), the sign of c2, A(N,n), the flux-independent baseline of mu4(Phi) and the many-cluster sector shift are not derived; the exchange coefficient (uniform hopping) depends only on C4 and is not a law in z, alpha_d(N,2) needs every side 3 or >=5; the doublon Hamiltonian derived for one doublon and its pi-periodicity exact only for that model; no many-pair stiffness, ODLRO, condensation, collective transport or superconductivity; projection, moment method and doublon form not claimed as new; machine-checked scope in App. F.

label: sec:discussion#bond-linearity
statement: With bond-dependent spin-independent Hermitian amplitudes (no on-site terms), $\mu_4(U\to\infty)$ is still exactly affine in $P_{\rm same}$ at fixed (N,n) on any finite graph: the closed-walk amplitude becomes the product of the walk's amplitudes, a spin-independent factor, so the walk decomposition holds with weighted walk sums; only the slope changes.
source: analytic_studies/05_mu4_exchange_topology.tex §8 (Bond-dependent amplitudes, rev. 2026-11-14); paper App. C (closed-walk amplitude lemma); checks/run_checks.py (sec:discussion#bond-linearity: random graph, complex amplitudes)

label: sec:futurework#mu2fluxblind
statement: Under the Peierls substitution $t_{ij}\to t_{ij}e^{iA_{ij}}$, $\mu_2(\Phi)=\mu_2(0)$ identically for any flux, because every contributing second-order path backtracks and acquires phase $e^{iA_{ij}}e^{-iA_{ij}}=1$.

label: sec:futurework#organizing
statement: Since $H_\infty(\Phi)$ is Hermitian, $\mu_4(\Phi)=\sum_{a,b}|(H_\infty^2(\Phi))_{ab}|^2$; a contribution reached by a single path is exactly flux-independent, and flux dependence requires at least two interfering paths to the same intermediate, with relative phase equal to the Wilson-loop phase of the closed loop they form (necessary but not sufficient).

label: sec:futurework#mechanisms
statement: The flux-sensitive four-hop mechanisms (the single-particle plaquette loop, the two ring-exchange channels and, for n>=3, the 3-cycle) all carry the same single harmonic: plaquette loop and 3-cycle are constructive at zero flux, proportional to (1+cos Phi), both exchange channels destructive, proportional to (1-cos Phi) for same spin and exactly flux-blind for opposite spin; there is no cos 2Phi anywhere, so the bare projected $\mu_4$ shows no charge-2e signature and exchange changes interference parity, not effective charge.

label: sec:futurework#alphaflux
statement: For n=2 on the LxL torus with L=3 or L>=5 and uniform plaquette flux $\Phi_\square=2\pi p/L^2$, the exchange coefficient is exactly $\alpha(N,2,\Phi)=-\frac{64}{N-1}\cos\Phi_\square$; it fails at L=4.
source: analytic_studies/10_flux_resolved_mu4_decomposition.tex §9.1 (revised 2026-11-13); checks/run_checks.py (sec:futurework: all L^2 fluxes at L=3, 5, 6, every third at L=7)

label: fig:mu4exchangeflux
statement: For n=2 on the 6x6 torus (N=36), the exact sparse-trace difference $\mu_4^{(2,0)}(\Phi)-\mu_4^{(1,1)}(\Phi)$ for a genuine Peierls (Hofstadter-type) Hamiltonian matches $-\frac{64}{N-1}\cos\Phi_\square$ to machine precision (RMS residual ~$10^{-14}$) with no fitted parameters; the spin-sector difference cancels the spin-blind orbital plaquette-loop contribution exactly.
source: mu4_flux_validation.py n2_flux_sweep(L=6) + make_figure -> results/mu4_flux_response.png (prints RMS residual)

label: sec:futurework#3cycle-nocos2
statement: At L=4 and L=5, sparse-trace evaluation with Peierls phases finds no cos 2Phi component in the 3-cycle's flux contribution, to the precision of the method, consistent with the constructive-interference derivation.
source: mu4_flux_validation.py n3_fourier_diagnostic(L=4) and n3_fourier_diagnostic(L=5) (cosine DFT of mu4(3,0)-mu4(2,1))

label: sec:futurework#nonclaim-retrace
statement: The flux-independent retrace baseline of $\mu_4(\Phi)$ (Type I's other sub-types together with Type II(a)) is only partially assembled into closed form for general N; what is resolved exactly, on LxL tori with L=3 or L>=5, is the flux factor of each mechanism ((1+cos Phi) for the plaquette loop and the 3-cycle, (1-cos Phi) for same-spin ring exchange), and the closed form of the exchange coefficient under flux is given for n=2 only.
source: analytic_studies/10_flux_resolved_mu4_decomposition.tex §5-§8 (flux factor of each mechanism), §9.1 (n=2 closed form), §9.2-§9.3 (baseline)

label: sec:futurework#difference-observable
statement: At $\Phi_\square=\pi$ the orbital and 3-cycle contributions vanish while the same-spin exchange contribution is maximal; for n=2 the difference $\mu_4^{(2,0)}(\Phi)-\mu_4^{(1,1)}(\Phi)$ cancels the spin-blind orbital background exactly, isolating exchange topology as a function of flux: a concrete diagnostic of exchange under flux.

label: eq:doublonSW
statement: For every finite graph, in the two-electron (single-doublon) sector, Peierls substitution followed by second-order Schrieffer-Wolff projection gives the doublon Hamiltonian $H_d^{(2)}(A)=\varepsilon_d^{(2)}\sum_in_i^d+t_d\sum_{\langle ij\rangle}(e^{2iA_{ji}}d_j^\dagger d_i+{\rm h.c.})$, $A_{ji}=-A_{ij}$, $t_d=2\lambda^2/U$: the hopping carries twice the bare link phase, there is no longer-range doublon hopping at this order, and the on-site shift ($8\lambda^2/U$; $2z\lambda^2/U$ at coordination z) is exactly flux-blind. The second-order terms are machine-checked; the Schrieffer-Wolff formula itself is tier A.
lean: doubledPeierlsPhase; doublonHoppingRange; doublonOnSiteShift; doublonOnSiteShiftTorus; doublonFirstOrderZero; pairHoppingHermitian
source: lean/HubbardMoments/Spec.lean:218,225,232,238,211,205; the second-order formula itself is tier A (analytic_studies/11 §1)

label: sec:futurework#gaugeforced
statement: The doubled phase is also forced by gauge covariance: matching $d_j^\dagger d_i\to e^{2i(\theta_i-\theta_j)}d_j^\dagger d_i$ by the transformation of $A_{ji}$ uniquely gives $e^{2iA_{ji}}$, given only that the hopping coefficient depends on its own bond phase alone.

label: sec:futurework#wilson-doubled
statement: Around one elementary plaquette, the doublon's enclosed Wilson phase is doubled, $\prod_\square e^{2iA_{ij}}=e^{2i\Phi_\square}$: a local statement, the doubled-phase analog of the orbital plaquette loop.

label: sec:futurework#twist-periodicity
statement: Under a global boundary twist theta, the one-doublon dispersion is $E_d(K;\theta)=\varepsilon_d+2t_d[\cos(K_x+2\theta/L)+\cos K_y]$ and ${\rm Spec}\,H_d(\theta+\pi)={\rm Spec}\,H_d(\theta)$ exactly for the second-order effective single-doublon Hamiltonian; the full two-electron spectrum is not pi-periodic.

label: sec:futurework#twist-uband
statement: The exact two-electron U-band under a boundary twist is pi-periodic up to deviations ~ (2 lambda)^L/U^(L-1) (L=6: about 1e-4 lambda at U=20 lambda, 3e-6 lambda at U=40 lambda; ratios between U=20 and 40 near 2^(L-1) at L=4,5,6) and matches the doubled-twist doublon dispersion to O(lambda^4/U^3) (8e-3 and 1e-3 lambda at L=6).

label: sec:futurework#doublonflux-numeric
statement: Against the exact flux-threaded finite-U two-electron Hubbard problem on the 6x6 torus, over all 36 quantized uniform fluxes, with no fitted parameters, the doubled-phase doublon prediction for the U-band outperforms an undoubled control in RMS residual by a factor of 12.5 at U=20 lambda and 48 at U=40 lambda (residual ratio 0.080 and 0.021; 0.280 at U=10 lambda and 0.0052 at U=80 lambda).
source: checks/slow_finite_U.py; evidence/2026-11-13-finite-U (doublon_flux_L6: residual ratio 0.2799, 0.0801, 0.0206, 0.0052 at U=10, 20, 40, 80; +t_d models); doublon_flux_validation.py flux_sweep

label: sec:futurework#oddL-bandwidth
statement: The zero-flux doublon bandwidth is $8t_d$ for even L but $4t_d[1+\cos(\pi/L)]$ for odd L, since K=(pi,pi) is then not an allowed momentum; the exact L=5 two-electron U-band converges to this odd-L value, not to $8t_d$, as U grows: ordinary momentum-grid discretization, not a many-body finite-size pathology.

label: fig:doublonflux
statement: On the 6x6 torus (N=36) at U=40 lambda, the top eigenvalue of the exact flux-threaded two-electron U-band follows the effective doublon model with doubled Peierls phase $t_de^{2iA_{ij}}$, not the undoubled control $t_de^{iA_{ij}}$, with no fitted parameters.

label: sec:futurework#nonclaim-exchangeflux
statement: The h/e flux sensitivity of the exchange loops demonstrates orbital/gauge sensitivity of the exchange topology and nothing more; a completely normal, non-superconducting system can have flux-sensitive closed paths.

label: sec:futurework#nonclaim-sc
statement: The paper establishes repulsive binding, a microscopic charge-2e gauge coupling and single-pair h/(2e) periodicity at leading order in 1/U only; it makes no claim about collective (non-additive) charge-2e transport, many-pair phase stiffness, off-diagonal long-range order, condensation or superconductivity, and the single-pair doublon flux response is a standard consequence of the effective Hamiltonian, not evidence of collective or superconducting behaviour.

label: app:dos#bessel
statement: For a d-dimensional hypercubic lattice with $E(\mathbf k)=-2\lambda\sum_i\cos k_i$, the DOS is exactly $\rho_d(E)=\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty\cos(Et)[J_0(2\lambda t)]^d\,dt$ for every d, with elementary closed forms for d=1 (inverse-square-root band edges) and d=2 (complete elliptic integral, log-divergent at the centre) and none for d>=3.

label: app:dos#kurtosis
statement: For isotropic hypercubic hopping in every dimension d, $\mu_2=2d\lambda^2$ and $\mu_4=12d^2\lambda^4-6d\lambda^4$, so the excess kurtosis is exactly $\gamma_2=-3/(2d)$: the non-Gaussianity is always present and vanishes as 1/d.

label: app:dos#aniso
statement: For $E=-2\sum_ic_i\cos k_i$ with independent uniform $k_i$ and arbitrary amplitudes $c_i$, $\rho(E)=\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty\cos(Et)\prod_iJ_0(2c_it)\,dt$, and exactly $\mathrm{Var}=2\sum c_i^2$, $\mu_4=-6\sum c_i^4+3\mathrm{Var}^2$ (per-term variance $2c_i^2$ and fourth cumulant $-6c_i^4$, both additive).

label: fig:dosfamily
statement: For the hypercubic DOS, van Hove structure visibly disappears from d=1 to d=4, and the variance-normalized DOS for d=4,5,6,8 is nearly indistinguishable from the unit Gaussian by eye, while the residual from the Gaussian stays clearly resolved and shrinks systematically with d.

label: app:mu4fpc#formula
statement: For every k<=N, the fourth moment of the sum of k values sampled without replacement from a zero-mean population $\{\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_N\}$ ($\sum_i\varepsilon_i=0$) is $\mu_4=P_4(p_1-7p_2+12p_3-6p_4)+3P_2^2(p_2-2p_3+p_4)$, with $P_m=\sum_i\varepsilon_i^m$, $p_m=k(k-1)\cdots(k-m+1)/[N(N-1)\cdots(N-m+1)]$ and $p_m=0$ for m>k.

label: app:mu4fpc#additivity
statement: For independent zero-mean X and Y (at U=0 the two spin species are independent, so a two-species spectrum is the sum of two single-species ones), $\mu_4(X+Y)=\mu_4(X)+\mu_4(Y)+6\,\mathrm{Var}(X)\mathrm{Var}(Y)$.

label: app:mu4fpc#validation
statement: The finite-population $\mu_4$ formula agrees exactly (rational arithmetic) with brute-force enumeration on a random centred toy population (k=2,3,4) and with the real L=4 single-particle spectrum.
source: checks/run_checks.py (app:mu4fpc: random centred population N=10, k=2,3,4, exact; tab:fpcexact: the L=4 band)

label: app:mu4walks#3cycle-multiplicity
statement: For the 3-cycle, exhaustive enumeration of $(H_\infty^2)_{ab}$ over all locally allowed intermediates from a={i,j,k} to b={i,k,m} finds exactly two routes with the same fermion sign, so $(H_\infty^2)_{ab}=-2\lambda^2$, twice the magnitude a single classical-path construction suggests; the exact sparse-trace numbers already sum over both routes.

label: app:mu4walks#mediators-208-200
statement: On a fully occupied plaquette at n=4 (a diagonal pair with both mediators occupied) the diagonal exchanges are blocked, and (H_inf^4)_aa = 208 - 4 x (number of same-spin bonds of the plaquette), from the edge channel around the outer neighbouring plaquettes: 208 with no same-spin bond, 200 with two, 192 with four (all spins equal), identical at L=5 and 6; no four-particle process contributes.

label: app:mu4walks#cubic
statement: On a periodic 3D simple-cubic lattice (z=6, N=27), exact sparse-trace evaluation gives $\alpha(27,2)=-96/13\approx-7.385$: twice the substitution $-16z/(N-1)=-48/13$, and not $-4z^2/(N-1)=-72/13$ either; direct enumeration shows each of the two channels doubles independently and supplies an equal half ($-1296\lambda^4$ of $-2592\lambda^4$).
source: checks/run_checks.py (app:mu4walks: 3x3x3 periodic, total and per channel, exact)

label: app:mu4walks#hypercubic
statement: For the d-dimensional periodic hypercubic lattice (z=2d) with every side 3 or >=5, the 4-cycles are the plaquettes, $C_4=Nd(d-1)/2$, so $\alpha_d(N,2)=-32d(d-1)/(N-1)=-16(d-1)z/(N-1)$; it reproduces $\alpha(27,2)=-96/13$ at d=3 and -48/31 on 5x5x5; each side of length 4 adds axis-ring 4-cycles, giving $-16[2d(d-1)+m]/(N-1)$ with m such sides (4x4x4: -80/21; 3x4: -80/11; 4x5: -80/19).

label: app:mu4walks#nonclaim-graphgeneral
statement: The exchange coefficient depends on the graph only through its number of 4-cycles: the square-lattice value -64/(N-1), written -16z/(N-1), is not a law in the coordination number (kagome, d=2 and z=4, has C4=0 and alpha=0; d=3 gives -96/13, not -48/13 or -72/13); the hypercubic form alpha_d(N,2) holds only on tori whose sides are all 3 or >=5.

label: app:mu4walks#L4anomaly
statement: On the 4x4 torus, $\alpha(16,2)=-32/5$ rather than the $-64/15$ of larger tori: its eight axis rings of length four are 4-cycles in addition to the 16 plaquettes, $C_4=24$, so Eq. alphaN gives -32/5; pair by pair, 16 extra diagonal-type pairs and an edge-channel value of -12 instead of -8.
source: analytic_studies/06_lattice_specificity_and_finite_size.tex §6-§8; checks/run_checks.py (sec:mu4exchange: by channel at L=4, 48 diagonal-type pairs at -8 and 32 edge pairs at -12; alpha(16,2) = -32/5)

label: app:mu4walks#n3plus-residual
statement: For n>2 the weight missed by independent blocking lies in the 2+1+1 hop class, where the four-hop 3-cycles live: a third particle next to a same-spin pair gives a clean, spin-dependent local value of $(H_\infty^4)_{aa}$ (180 same-spin and 186 opposite-spin on a mediator of a diagonal pair; 180 and 182 on a plaquette corner next to an edge pair), identical at L=5 and L=6; summed with the spin-averaging weights, the 3-cycles give the second term of Eq. alphaN.

label: fig:walktypes
statement: Schematic of the four-hop closed-walk types of $\mu_4(U\to\infty)$ on one plaquette (Types I(i)-(iv), II(a), II(b) diagonal and edge, III), each with the number of routes to a common two-hop intermediate, its interference at zero flux, its flux factor (none, $1+\cos\Phi_\square$, $1-\cos\Phi_\square$) and its spin condition.
source: schematic drawn in TikZ in manuscript/fig_walktypes.tex (no script), shared with analytic_studies/10_flux_resolved_mu4_decomposition.tex §4; content from analytic_studies/05_mu4_exchange_topology.tex §3, analytic_studies/10_flux_resolved_mu4_decomposition.tex §4-§8, paper App. C and §8

label: app:SW#tJ
statement: Up to the overall 1/U and normalization, $-V=-T_1^\dagger T_1$ is the standard second-order strong-coupling operator of the Hubbard-to-t-J transformation: Heisenberg superexchange $J\sum_{\langle ij\rangle}(\mathbf S_i\cdot\mathbf S_j-\frac14n_in_j)$ with $J=4\lambda^2/U$ (diagonal and spin-flip pieces) plus the correlated three-site hopping term.

label: app:numerics#signrule
statement: With fermion operators satisfying the canonical anticommutation relations, for any k and any orbital ordering, moving the rank-m fermion of a sorted k-tuple to an empty site a gives sign $(-1)^m(-1)^p$, with p the number of remaining occupied sites below a; the resulting $H_\infty$ is Hermitian with single hops of modulus lambda.

label: app:numerics#signrule-crossval
statement: The sorted-tuple sign rule was verified Hermitian for k=2, cross-validated against an independent Jordan-Wigner bit-string implementation on 4000 random moves (k=1..8, 12 sites) with zero mismatches, and, for a single species with k=4 at L=4, the moments mu2, mu4 of the operator built with it agree exactly (rational arithmetic) with the free-fermion values.
source: checks/run_checks.py (app:numerics: sorted-tuple rule vs an independent Jordan-Wigner bit-string implementation, 4000 random moves, k=1..8; H_inf symmetric); the k=4 free-fermion check is sec:fermistats in checks/run_checks.py (mu4(U=0)=mu4(U=inf), exact)

label: app:numerics#sparse-method
statement: All U=infinity and Schrieffer-Wolff moments are computed by exact sparse matrix products ($\mathrm{Tr}H^2$ from the diagonal of $H^2$, $\mathrm{Tr}H^4=\sum_{ab}(H^2)_{ab}^2$ for symmetric H), never diagonalization, keeping every reported moment exact to the printed digits and tractable up to $D_0\sim10^5$ in well under a second per composition.
source: uinf_traces_sparse.py moments_via_traces; sw_correction.py sw_moments; mu4_flux_validation.py mu2_mu4_sparse

label: fig:kgridUband
statement: At U=10,15,20,50 lambda, the exact two-electron U-band from a direct relative-coordinate K-grid scan (L_rel=21, 48x48 K-points) agrees with the parameter-free second-order prediction $\rho_{2D}(E-\varepsilon_d;t_d)$, with no fitted parameters, from moderate coupling into the asymptotic doublon regime.

label: app:lean#scope
statement: Not machine-checked: the Schrieffer-Wolff expansion itself at second and third order (hence c2); the identification of U=0 many-body energies with sums of the energies of distinct single-particle states and of the band with plane waves; every fourth-moment coefficient (alpha(N,n), alpha_d(N,2)) and the spin-averaging step, hence the exact linearity of $\mu_4(\infty)$; the physical identification of the formalized fermion operators beyond the CAR; all spectral, DOS and finite-U numerics are independent of the formalization.
